requirements.requirement: Run a healthy three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: Cluster bootstrapped via systemd on all three nodes; member list shows all three 'started'; endpoint health reports all three healthy; five /app/* keys written and confirmed present on node1, node2, and node3.

requirements.requirement: Simulate permanent, unrecoverable loss of the node3 member while preserving cluster quorum
requirements.summary: node3's etcd service was stopped/disabled, its member (52ba345fe2656a9a) was removed from the raft configuration via `member remove`, and its data directory was wiped with rm -rf. The remaining node1/node2 endpoints reported healthy (2/2) immediately after removal, confirming quorum was preserved throughout.

requirements.requirement: Replace the lost member with a working member on node3 so the cluster returns to three healthy members with existing keys intact
requirements.summary: A fresh member (7c13a4e7ad88e8ba) was registered via `member add`, node3's systemd unit was rewritten with initial-cluster-state=existing and started, and the new instance joined successfully. Endpoint health and member list both show 3/3 healthy started members, and `get /app --prefix` on the new node3 member returns all five original application keys, confirming full resync.

overall_summary: The executor stood up a genuine 3-member etcd cluster on node1/node2/node3, wrote application keys and confirmed their replication, then faithfully simulated an unrecoverable loss of the node3 member (stop, member remove, data wipe) while keeping the surviving two-node cluster at quorum. It replaced the lost member with a newly registered, distinct member on node3 (initial-cluster-state=existing) and directly demonstrated the cluster returning to 3/3 healthy with all five original keys resynced onto the new member. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also executed and evidenced end-to-end on all three nodes: pre-restart boot IDs and healthy baselines, a reboot acknowledgement causing session disconnection, distinct post-restart boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots), and full etcd/cluster/data recovery after each restart, including confirmation that node3's replaced member (7c13a4e7ad88e8ba) survived its own reboot in the membership list. The only hygiene gap is leftover installer artifacts (etcd tarball/extracted dir) in /tmp on all three nodes, a minor, low-risk residue rather than a functional defect.
limitations: Restart-protocol evidence, while thorough and cross-checked against fixed boot-identity snapshots, is not itself part of the public task contract; it is assessed here only to inform confidence and hygiene, not as a scored task requirement.
Evidence for command outcomes relies on captured stdout/return codes only; no independent verification beyond the provided trace and snapshots was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. Nearly all state-changing commands (binary install, hosts/user/firewall setup, systemd unit writes, cluster bootstrap, key writes, member remove/wipe/add for the simulated failure and replacement, and the three sequential node restarts) map directly to the task's replacement objective or the mandatory restart protocol. One nonzero-exit command (cmd-85a1f2bb28cf4167, node1 initial `systemctl enable --now etcd` reporting a timeout) is expected discovery during 3-node initial cluster bootstrap — the service was confirmed running seconds later (cmd-790d663d169c44d5), so it caused no lasting issue. The lifecycle diff shows the etcd release tarball and extracted directory (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz, /tmp/etcd-v3.7.1-linux-amd64/*) were left behind in /tmp on all three nodes after the executor finished — a bounded, low-risk residue from a necessary installation step that was never cleaned up. No failed services, unnecessary mutations unrelated to the task, or weakened security controls were observed; package-health and failed-services checks are clean on all nodes both before and after.
